1	//! Share links — hand one indexed corpus to someone who has nothing else.
2	//!
3	//! `xerj brain <folder>` leaves the owner with a node whose only credential is
4	//! the admin key. Sending a friend that key hands them the whole node; minting
5	//! them a scoped key by hand means explaining `role_descriptors`. A share is
6	//! the one-command version of the second thing: the owner names an index (and
7	//! optionally the brain whose links sit beside it), gets a link plus a
8	//! passcode, and the guest who opens the link and types the passcode is
9	//! handed a **scoped, read-only, expiring** API key that reaches exactly the
10	//! indices the share names — and nothing else on the node.
11	//!
12	//! ## What is stored, and what is not
13	//!
14	//! Records live in `<data_dir>/shares.json` beside `api_keys.json` — same 0600
15	//! atomic writer ([`xerj_engine::engine::write_secret_file_atomic`]). They are
16	//! deliberately *not* documents in a reserved index: a file is reachable by no
17	//! search, `_cat`, snapshot, alias or `_delete_by_query` route, so there is no
18	//! second copy of the reserved-namespace exception list to keep in sync.
19	//!
20	//! Nothing in a record is a usable secret:
21	//! - the share id (the token in the link) is stored as a **SHA-256 digest**;
22	//!   the plaintext exists only in the create response and in the link;
23	//! - the passcode is stored as an **Argon2id** hash. Unlike a minted API-key
24	//!   secret (244 bits of CSPRNG, see `xerj_engine::secret_hash` for why that
25	//!   one is a fast hash) a passcode is short and may have been chosen by a
26	//!   human, so an offline guess is a real threat and a slow hash is the right
27	//!   tool. It is verified once per claim, on a rate-limited route, so the cost
28	//!   never lands on the request path;
29	//! - the guest's API key is **minted at claim time**, one per claim, expiring
30	//!   when the share expires. The record keeps only the minted key *ids* so a
31	//!   revoke can invalidate every key the share ever produced. No credential
32	//!   is ever written to the share file.
33	//!
34	//! ## Who may do what
35	//!
36	//! | Route | Who |
37	//! |---|---|
38	//! | `POST /_share`, `GET /_share`, `DELETE /_share/{handle}` | superuser only (the admin key) — a scoped or unscoped key gets 403 |
39	//! | `POST /_share/claim` | **nobody in particular** — it is exempt from authentication (`auth::is_share_claim_path`) the way `/v1/metrics` is for the scrape token, and rate-limited per source address and per share instead |
40	//!
41	//! The claim route is the only unauthenticated door that hands out a
42	//! credential, so it is narrow on purpose: one exact path, `POST` only, a body
43	//! capped at [`MAX_CLAIM_BODY_BYTES`], a sliding-window throttle,
44	//! `Cache-Control: no-store` on every answer, and every outcome — success,
45	//! wrong passcode, exhausted, expired, revoked, unknown, throttled — in the
46	//! audit log with the source address.
47	//!
48	//! ## The share id is never part of a request path
49	//!
50	//! The claim body is `{id, passcode}`. The first cut put the id in the path
51	//! (`POST /_share/{id}/claim`), and the guest page's care to keep the id in the
52	//! URL *fragment* was undone one request later: a request path is exactly what
53	//! an access log records. With `logging.access_log = true` this node wrote the
54	//! id to `server.log` twice per claim, and any reverse proxy or tunnel in front
55	//! of it logged the same line (review of PR #947, reproduced 2026-09-19). A
56	//! body is in none of those logs. `DELETE /_share/{handle}` takes the public
57	//! handle, which opens nothing. It also accepts the full id, for an API caller
58	//! who kept only that — such a call puts the id in its own request path, which
59	//! is why `xerj share --revoke` sends only the handle.
60	//!
61	//! ## The two throttles, and why a tunnel does not break them
62	//!
63	//! - A claim against a **known** share is charged to that share's window
64	//!   ([`SHARE_PER_MINUTE`] / [`SHARE_PER_HOUR`]), from anywhere. This is the
65	//!   passcode lockout, and it does not depend on knowing who is asking.
66	//! - A claim against an **unknown** id is charged to the source address's
67	//!   window ([`IP_PER_MINUTE`] / [`IP_PER_HOUR`]). It bounds junk traffic and
68	//!   the audit lines it writes.
69	//!
70	//! They are deliberately *not* stacked. The first cut charged the source
71	//! window before looking the share up, which is fine on a directly exposed
72	//! node and wrong behind `xerj share --tunnel`: every request a tunnel (or any
73	//! reverse proxy on the same host) delivers arrives from `127.0.0.1`, so all
74	//! guests shared one source bucket, and ten junk requests a minute from anyone
75	//! who had found the hostname answered every real guest with `429` — a
76	//! one-line denial of service on the feature. The fix is not to believe
77	//! `X-Forwarded-For`: a direct client writes that header itself (#76 S5-4),
78	//! and an unconfigured node believes nobody. It is to stop the collapsed
79	//! bucket from mattering: a real share id is governed by its own window, which
80	//! no amount of junk can touch, and junk is governed by the source window,
81	//! where collapsing every tunnel client into one bucket only makes the bound
82	//! tighter.
83	//!
84	//! Operators who want each guest's real address — in the audit log and as the
85	//! junk-traffic key — declare the proxy the usual way,
86	//! `server.trusted_proxies = ["127.0.0.1", "::1"]`; then, and only then,
87	//! `X-Forwarded-For` is read, right to left (see [`ClaimSource`]). IPv6
88	//! sources are keyed by their /64, since one host is routinely handed a whole
89	//! /64 to rotate through.
90	//!
91	//! ## An open node cannot share
92	//!
93	//! With authentication off (`--insecure`, `auth.enabled = false`, or no admin
94	//! key) every request is [`Principal::Superuser`], so a "scoped, read-only"
95	//! guest key would restrict nothing. `POST /_share` and the claim route answer
96	//! `409` there rather than hand out a credential that promises a boundary the
97	//! node is not enforcing.
98	//!
99	//! ## What a guest can reach
100	//!
101	//! The minted key carries one role, named `share:<handle>`: `read` on the
102	//! share's `indices` plus, when a brain is named, `read` on that brain's edges
103	//! index (`authz::brain_edges_index`). Two things then confine it:
104	//!
105	//! 1. the index grants — the same per-index authorization every scoped key
106	//!    gets, in the middleware and again in the engine's index funnel;
107	//! 2. a **route allow-list** that applies to share guests only
108	//!    (`authz::guest_route_allowed`, keyed on [`GUEST_ROLE_PREFIX`]):
109	//!    `_search`, `_count`, `_msearch`, `_mget`, `_mapping`, `_field_caps` and
110	//!    `GET _doc/{id}` on the granted indices, and
111	//!    `GET /_graph/{brain}/ego|overview`. An ordinary scoped key is given a
112	//!    *filtered* view of `_cat`, `_cluster/*`, `_nodes` and friends because
113	//!    Kibana needs one; a guest is given none of it. No `scroll`, no `_pit`,
114	//!    no `_async_search` either — nothing that parks state on the owner's
115	//!    machine.
116	//!
117	//! The `autoindex-catalog` index is **never** granted, and cannot be named in a
118	//! share ([`CATALOG_INDEX`], refused by `validate_share_index`): it lists every
119	//! corpus on the node, the engine has no document-level security to filter it
120	//! with, and the guest page already receives the index name directly.
121	//!
122	//! Every response to a guest key is `Cache-Control: no-store`
123	//! (`authz::authz_middleware`): it is somebody's documents, on its way through
124	//! whatever proxy or tunnel the owner put in front of the node.

396	    /// Charge one claim attempt against `key`. `Err` when over either window.
397	    /// Same sliding-window shape as the console's auth limiter
398	    /// (`xerj-console-api::auth::rate_limit`), re-implemented here because
399	    /// that one is bound to `ConsoleState` and this crate must not depend on
400	    /// the console.
401	    fn charge(
402	        &self,
403	        key: &str,
404	        per_minute: u32,
405	        per_hour: u32,
406	        now_ms: u64,
407	    ) -> Result<(), Throttled> {
408	        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
409	        if self
410	            .charges
411	            .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
412	            .is_multiple_of(PRUNE_EVERY)
413	        {
414	            self.windows
415	                .retain(|_, w| now_ms.saturating_sub(w.start_ms) < WINDOW_HOUR_MS);
416	        }
417	        // Bounded state for an unauthenticated route: once the table is full,
418	        // addresses it has not seen yet are throttled as one.
419	        // Only source keys collapse: share keys are bounded by the number of
420	        // shares, which only the superuser can create.
421	        let key = if key.starts_with("ip:")
422	            && self.windows.len() >= MAX_WINDOWS
423	            && !self.windows.contains_key(&format!("{key}:m"))
424	        {
425	            "ip:overflow"
426	        } else {
427	            key
428	        };
429	        for (suffix, window_ms, limit) in [
430	            ("m", WINDOW_MIN_MS, per_minute),
431	            ("h", WINDOW_HOUR_MS, per_hour),
432	        ] {
433	            let k = format!("{key}:{suffix}");
434	            let mut w = self.windows.entry(k).or_insert(RateWindow {
435	                count: 0,
436	                start_ms: now_ms,
437	            });
438	            if now_ms.saturating_sub(w.start_ms) > window_ms {
439	                *w = RateWindow {
440	                    count: 0,
441	                    start_ms: now_ms,
442	                };
443	            }
444	            w.count = w.count.saturating_add(1);
445	            if w.count > limit {
446	                return Err(Throttled {
447	                    retry_after_secs: (w.start_ms + window_ms).saturating_sub(now_ms) / 1000 + 1,
448	                    first_in_window: w.count == limit + 1,
449	                });
450	            }
451	        }
452	        Ok(())
453	    }
454	}

491	/// Alphabet for generated passcodes: lowercase + digits with the four
492	/// look-alikes (`0/o`, `1/l`, plus `i`) removed, 31 symbols. Eight of them is
493	/// ~39.6 bits, which with [`SHARE_PER_HOUR`] guesses an hour is out of reach
494	/// online, and which is what the human on the other end has to type.
495	const PASSCODE_ALPHABET: &[u8] = b"abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789";

497	/// `xxxx-xxxx` from the alphabet above.
498	pub fn generate_passcode() -> String {
499	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(9);
500	    let mut rng = rand::rngs::OsRng;
501	    for i in 0..8 {
502	        if i == 4 {
503	            out.push('-');
504	        }
505	        // Rejection-free: 31 does not divide 256, so draw a u32 and take the
506	        // modulo of a much larger range; the bias is < 2^-24 per symbol.
507	        let n = rng.next_u32() as usize % PASSCODE_ALPHABET.len();
508	        out.push(PASSCODE_ALPHABET[n] as char);
509	    }
510	    out
511	}

532	fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
533	    const T: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
534	    let mut s = String::with_capacity(bytes.len() * 2);
535	    for b in bytes {
536	        s.push(T[(b >> 4) as usize] as char);
537	        s.push(T[(b & 15) as usize] as char);
538	    }
539	    s

542	fn constant_time_eq(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
543	    if a.len() != b.len() {
544	        return false;
545	    }
546	    let mut diff = 0u8;
547	    for (x, y) in a.iter().zip(b) {
548	        diff |= x ^ y;
549	    }
550	    diff == 0
551	}

569	pub fn parse_expires_in(spec: &str) -> Option<u64> {
570	    let s = spec.trim();

584	/// Is `name` a concrete index a share may grant? Same alphabet the engine
585	/// accepts, minus anything that is a pattern or a list — a grant must name
586	/// exactly what it grants — and minus the reserved namespace, which is only
587	/// reachable through `brain`.
588	fn validate_share_index(name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
589	    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 255 {
590	        return Err("index name must be 1–255 characters".into());
591	    }
592	    if name.starts_with(crate::authz::RESERVED_INDEX_PREFIX) {
593	        return Err(format!(
594	            "index `{name}` is in the reserved .xerj-memory-* namespace; share a brain with `brain` instead"
595	        ));
596	    }
597	    // Every dot-index is the node's own: `.xerj_sessions`, `.xerj_api_tokens`,
598	    // `.xerj_passkeys` and `.xerj_magic_links` are credential stores, and
599	    // `.xerj_audit` records who connected from where. The check above named only
600	    // the memory namespace, so a share on any of these was accepted — found by
601	    // the first live run (2026-09-18), which minted a guest link onto the audit
602	    // log. A share grants a *user's* corpus, and no user index starts with a dot,
603	    // so the rule is the whole prefix rather than a list that has to be kept in
604	    // step with every system index added later.
605	    if name.starts_with('.') {
606	        return Err(format!(
607	            "index `{name}` is a system index and cannot be shared; a share names one of your own indices"
608	        ));
609	    }
610	    if name.starts_with('_') {
611	        return Err(format!("index `{name}` is not an index name"));
612	    }
613	    // The catalog describes EVERY corpus on the node. The docs said it was
614	    // "never granted" while `xerj share autoindex-catalog` minted a guest key
615	    // that read all of it (review of PR #947). A guest is handed one corpus;
616	    // the list of the others is not part of it, and there is no
617	    // document-level security to filter the list down.
618	    if name == CATALOG_INDEX {
619	        return Err(format!(
620	            "index `{name}` is the autoindex catalog: it describes every corpus on this \
621	             node, not one of them, so it cannot be shared. Share the corpus index itself \
622	             (`xerj autoindex map` lists them)"
623	        ));
624	    }
625	    for c in name.chars() {
626	        if c.is_whitespace()
627	            || matches!(
628	                c,
629	                '*' | ',' | '/' | '\\' | '?' | '"' | '<' | '>' | '|' | '#'
630	            )
631	        {
632	            return Err(format!(
633	                "index `{name}` contains `{c}`; a share names concrete indices, not patterns"
634	            ));
635	        }
636	        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() {
637	            return Err(format!("index `{name}` must be lowercase"));
638	        }
639	    }
640	    Ok(())
641	}

742	/// The address a claim came from, for the rate limiter and the audit line.
743	///
744	/// The TCP peer, from `ConnectInfo` — the caller cannot forge it. Forwarding
745	/// headers are believed only when the peer is one of the operator's declared
746	/// `server.trusted_proxies`, walking `X-Forwarded-For` right-to-left past
747	/// other declared proxies (the same reading as the console's `client_ip`,
748	/// #76 S5-4). With no `ConnectInfo` at all — a router driven by `oneshot` in

753	#[axum::async_trait]
754	impl FromRequestParts<AppState> for ClaimSource {
755	    type Rejection = std::convert::Infallible;
756	
757	    async fn from_request_parts(
758	        parts: &mut Parts,
759	        state: &AppState,
760	    ) -> Result<Self, Self::Rejection> {
761	        let peer = parts
762	            .extensions
763	            .get::<ConnectInfo<SocketAddr>>()
764	            .map(|c| xerj_common::net::canonical_ip(c.0.ip()));
765	        let Some(peer) = peer else {
766	            return Ok(ClaimSource("unknown".to_string()));
767	        };
768	        let trusted = xerj_common::net::TrustedProxies::parse(&state.config.server.trusted_proxies)
769	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| xerj_common::net::TrustedProxies::none());
770	        if !trusted.contains(&peer) {
771	            return Ok(ClaimSource(peer.to_string()));
772	        }
773	        let elements: Vec<&str> = parts
774	            .headers
775	            .get_all("x-forwarded-for")
776	            .iter()
777	            .filter_map(|v| v.to_str().ok())
778	            .flat_map(|v| v.split(','))
779	            .collect();
780	        for element in elements.iter().rev() {
781	            match xerj_common::net::parse_forwarded_element(element) {
782	                Some(ip) => {
783	                    let ip: IpAddr = xerj_common::net::canonical_ip(ip);
784	                    if !trusted.contains(&ip) {
785	                        return Ok(ClaimSource(ip.to_string()));
786	                    }
787	                }
788	                None => break,
789	            }
790	        }
791	        Ok(ClaimSource(peer.to_string()))
792	    }
793	}

# 5. Passcode comparison and brute-force throttling

**Constant time — yes, twice over.**

1. The passcode itself: `/root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/share.rs:523-530`:
```rust

    let Ok(parsed) = PasswordHash::new(stored) else {
        return false;
    };
    Argon2::default()
        .verify_password(presented.as_bytes(), &parsed)
        .is_ok()
}
```

No `==`, no `str::eq` on any secret anywhere in the file. Pinned by `passcode_hash_verifies_only_the_right_code_and_never_stores_plaintext` (share.rs:1426-1435), including the unparsable-stored-hash and empty-passcode cases.
